title: Shortcircuit gating preflight notes - 2027-03-22
content:
Attendees: Priya Patel (owner), Diego Ramos, Maya Chen, Noah Turner, Hannah Lee, Benji Cole (SRE drop-in)

Meeting goal: Rapid preflight and decision record for the "shortcircuit" feature-flag gating flow. This flag is intended to short-circuit the analytics-heavy UI panel (callout panel + live token counts) for premium low-latency routes when latency SLOs are at risk. We ran a small experiment last week; this meeting captures learnings, defines safe canary steps, and assigns owners for the rollout rehearsal.

Background / context:
- Feature: shortcircuit-panel reduces client-side telemetry calls and defers heavy event enrichment to async workers. Implemented as a server-side gate that returns a lightweight panel payload (no live token counts, no heavy embeddings).
- Motivation: several high-throughput Hosted API customers observed p95 UI latency regressions when panel enrichment coincided with sudden burst traffic. Shortcircuit reduces per-request CPU on panel path and bypasses KV cache warmups for non-critical UX.
- Relevant artifacts: PR #984 (console frontend + gate), CONSOLE-4123 (Jira for gating strategy), internal runbook draft.

Notes from the experiment (2027-03-18 to 2027-03-21):
- Synthetic load: 60m run at 1.5x typical concurrent sessions using harness 'tele-harness-v2'. No increased error budget observed.
- Observed tradeoffs: average end-to-end panel render latency improved ~38ms for gated requests; however, synthetic telemetry counts for enrichment events dropped by ~72% (expected). One downstream consumer (session-replay service) saw a 15% drop in enrichment events and raised a minor alert (resolved via buffer adjustment).
- User-facing regression: none detected in canary session QA (10 test cases). Small visual mismatch reported if the panel expected live token peek; UX agreed to show micro-copy 'live metrics paused — low-latency mode'.

Open questions resolved in meeting:
- Q: Are there any compliance or audit objections to deferring enrichment? A: Security & compliance consulted; OK for non-sensitive telemetry. Audit logs for decision points must still be written. (Action: add audit event for gate evaluation.)
- Q: Does the gate change quota accounting paths? A: No — billing tokens are calculated upstream. Gate only affects enrichment layer.

Risks identified:
- Telemetry consumers who rely on immediate enrichment may temporarily undercount; risk mitigation: backfill pipeline + small buffer queue.
- If canary routing misconfigures, we may inadvertently shortcircuit premium customers. Mitigation: strict allowlist per-tenant and automated validation script.
- UX confusion for power-users expecting live metrics. Mitigation: copy + tooltip + short product banner.

Decisions / agreement:
1) Proceed with a staged canary: 0.5% global traffic -> 5% tenant subset by quota -> 10% selected customers listed in allowlist -> expand 24 hours at each step with automated checks.
2) Add audit event at gate evaluation (CONSOLE-4123).
3) Add a 'shortcircuit-mode' label to all downstream telemetry so backfills can filter.
4) Require SRE run synthetic-load rehearsal (game day) before any wider expansion.

Preflight checklist (must pass all):
- [ ] Allowlist script reviewed and tested locally (owner: Noah) — due 2027-03-24
- [ ] Audit event instrumentation merged and shipped (owner: Priya / PR #984) — due 2027-03-23
- [ ] QA visual copy + tooltip approved by UX (owner: Maya) — due 2027-03-24
- [ ] Synthetic load rehearsal scheduled with SRE (owner: Benji) — scheduled 2027-03-25, backup 2027-03-26
- [ ] Backfill pipeline smoke test (owner: Diego) — due 2027-03-26
- [ ] Canary observability dashboard (latency p50/p95, errors, missing-enrichment-rate, telemetry-drop-rate) live and red/amber/green thresholds set (owner: Hannah) — due 2027-03-23

Rollback triggers (automated):
- p95 panel latency increases > 20% vs baseline for 10m window
- client-visible error rate > 0.5% on gated path for 5m
- telemetry-drop-rate > 40% for more than 30m for a non-exempt tenant
- unexpected increase in downstream queue depth > 2x baseline for 15m
If any trigger fires, the automated rollout controller should revert flag to previous state and page the on-call. (Runbook reference linked.)

Action items (owner, task, due):
- Priya: merge audit-event changes into PR #984 and coordinate release with CI gating. Due 2027-03-23.
- Noah: finish allowlist validator script and add small unit tests. Due 2027-03-24.
- Maya: finalize UX copy and prepare screenshot checklist for QA; coordinate small user announcement. Due 2027-03-24.
- Diego: run backfill pipeline smoke test and confirm that session-replay consumer accepts buffered events. Due 2027-03-26.
- Hannah: create canary dashboard tiles, set automated checks + pager thresholds. Due 2027-03-23.
- Benji (SRE): schedule and run game-day rehearsal (synthetic + small chaos: delayed enrichment, 5% error injection). Test automated rollback. Rehearsal 2027-03-25.

Follow-ups / sync plan:
- Quick async update to console-rollouts Slack channel after each preflight item completion.
- Post-game-day brief (30m) to capture any hidden failure modes; owners invited: all collaborators + on-call.
- If all preflight gates pass, prepare canary rollout kickoff 2027-03-29 (tentative).

Notes to self / scratch ideas (informal):
- Consider an intermediate mode: 'degraded enrichment' where we sample enrichment payloads for specific tenants — helps with both UX and telemetry fidelity.
- Explore small server-side cache for 'last-known-live-metrics' to show to power users without re-triggering full enrichment.

Appendix (quick links & commands):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/984
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/CONSOLE-4123
- Runbook draft: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/shortcircuit-gating
- Allowlist test (local): scripts/allowlist-validator --sample tenants.json

End of notes.

-- Priya
